nodes.label: Badge URL generator
nodes.detail: The badge dialog on the monitor details screen. Pick a type, a colour and a period; it assembles the URL, previews it with an and offers a copy field for pasting elsewhere

nodes.label: Entry point check
nodes.detail: Mounted right as the SPA starts, it calls /api/entry-page and routes to either the dashboard or a status page

nodes.label: Tag UI on the monitor form
nodes.detail: The tag management component embedded in the monitor edit screen (EditMonitor.vue). It fetches the existing tags and opens the new-tag input

nodes.label: Save the tag changes
nodes.detail: Applies the staged tags to the monitor. New ones go through addTag then addMonitorTag; removals go through deleteMonitorTag

nodes.label: Add tag button in settings
nodes.detail: The "Add New Tag" button on Settings > Tags. It opens an empty TagEditDialog to create a standalone tag

nodes.label: Save in the tag edit dialog
nodes.detail: Checks for a duplicate name, creates the tag with addTag, and also sends addMonitorTag and friends for the monitors being added or removed

nodes.label: External badge viewer
nodes.detail: Wherever the copied badge URL is embedded as an — a README, a status page or anything else outside the app

nodes.label: Prometheus server
nodes.detail: The external monitoring stack that scrapes /metrics on a schedule with Basic auth to collect prom-client metrics

nodes.label: GET badge/status
nodes.detail: The API that turns a monitor's status into an SVG badge. Cached 5 minutes; a private or missing monitor returns N/A

nodes.label: GET badge/uptime
nodes.detail: The API that turns the uptime over a period into an SVG badge. 24h by default, cached 5 minutes; private returns N/A

nodes.label: GET badge/response
nodes.detail: The API that turns the latest heartbeat's response time (ping) into an SVG badge. Cached 5 minutes; private or no ping returns N/A

nodes.label: GET badge/cert-exp
nodes.detail: The API that turns the days left on the TLS certificate (or its expiry date) into an SVG badge. Cached 5 minutes, judged in three bands

nodes.label: GET entry-page
nodes.detail: Decides whether the requested host name matches a status page's custom domain and returns the destination as JSON

nodes.label: GET metrics
nodes.detail: The endpoint that returns prom-client metrics as text, behind Basic auth (an API key or a user)

nodes.label: socket getTags
nodes.detail: The Socket.io event that returns every tag for the signed-in user

nodes.label: socket addTag
nodes.detail: The Socket.io event that inserts a new tag (name / colour) into the tag table

nodes.label: socket editTag
nodes.detail: The Socket.io event that updates the name and colour of the tag with the given tag.id

nodes.label: socket addMonitorTag
nodes.detail: The Socket.io event that links an existing tag (with an optional value) to a monitor

nodes.label: Check login
nodes.detail: Throws when socket.userID is missing — the shared guard for every socket event that requires a login

nodes.label: Basic auth for the API
nodes.detail: Depending on the disableAuth and apiKeysEnabled settings, it does Basic auth with either an API key or a normal user

nodes.label: Is the monitor public?
nodes.detail: Joins monitor_group with group and checks whether any group the monitor belongs to has public=1

nodes.label: Make the SVG badge
nodes.detail: Builds the badge SVG string from the label, value, colour and style with the badge-maker library

nodes.label: Get the latest heartbeat
nodes.detail: Finds the single newest heartbeat for a monitor_id by MAX(id)

nodes.label: Prepare the preload data
nodes.detail: Preloads and shapes notifications, tags, maintenance state and more for several monitors at once

nodes.label: Fetch monitor tags in bulk
nodes.detail: Joins monitor_tag with tag to fetch the tags (with name and colour) for a set of monitor IDs in one query

nodes.label: Get the uptime calculator
nodes.detail: Returns the UptimeCalculator cached in memory per monitor (creating it if there is none)

nodes.label: Work out the data for a period
nodes.detail: A pure computation of the uptime and average ping for a period (24h and so on) from the in-memory aggregates

nodes.label: Initialize Prometheus
nodes.detail: Sanitizes every tag name into a label candidate and creates the monitor_status and other Gauges once, at startup

nodes.label: Load the custom domain table
nodes.detail: Joins status_page with status_page_cname and loads the domain-to-slug table into memory

nodes.label: Re-send the monitor info
nodes.detail: Builds the monitor's latest data and sends updateMonitorIntoList to that user's sockets

nodes.label: Rebuild the monitor list
nodes.detail: Finds the monitors matching user_id and shapes them with toJSON, including the preloaded tags and the rest

nodes.label: Cache for 5 minutes
nodes.detail: The apicache middleware. It caches a GET of the same URL for five minutes and, on a hit, never runs the handler

nodes.label: Server bootstrap
nodes.detail: The startup IIFE that, once the DB is connected, reads entryPage, loads the domain table, initializes Prometheus and so on, in order

nodes.label: Monitor
nodes.detail: The table defining the monitored targets

nodes.label: Heartbeat
nodes.detail: The table recording each monitor's check results (status / ping / time and more)

nodes.label: Tag
nodes.detail: The master table holding tag names and colours

nodes.label: Monitor-tag link
nodes.detail: The table holding the many-to-many relation between monitors and tags (with a value)

nodes.label: TLS certificate info
nodes.detail: Holds the latest TLS certificate info (JSON) per monitor

nodes.label: Status page
nodes.detail: The table defining the public status pages

nodes.label: Custom domain
nodes.detail: Holds the custom domains (CNAMEs) attached to a status page

nodes.label: Group (public flag)
nodes.detail: Holds the grouping of monitors and the public flag (whether badges and the status page may show them)

nodes.label: Monitor-group membership
nodes.detail: Holds which monitors belong to which group

flows.title: Fetch the status badge as an image
flows.trigger: The live preview in the badge dialog, or a badge image pasted on an outside site, loading /api/badge/:id/status

steps.label: Live preview through the in the dialog
Copy the URL and paste it on an outside site
Find the newest row by MAX(id)
Pick the colour and wording from the status

notes: On a cache hit isMonitorPublic and the rest never run again, so making a monitor private has no effect for the rest of the 5-minute window
The live preview goes through exactly the same URL and path (api.http.badge_status) as an external embed

flows.title: Fetch the uptime badge
flows.trigger: The live preview in the badge dialog, or a badge image pasted on an outside site, loading /api/badge/:id/uptime/:duration?

steps.label: Live preview through the in the dialog
Copy the URL and paste it on an outside site
Work out the value for the period
Return the uptime and the average ping
Turn the uptime into a colour and a label

notes: The colour can be overridden with the color query. By default it comes from the uptime through percentageToColor (server/util-server.js:692), which this flow does not expand
The UptimeCalculator loads from the stat_ tables on first access and keeps the data in memory. Its internals are outside the scope of this map

flows.title: Fetch the response time badge
flows.trigger: The live preview in the badge dialog, or a badge image pasted on an outside site, loading /api/badge/:id/response

steps.label: Live preview through the in the dialog
Copy the URL and paste it on an outside site
Find the newest row by MAX(id)
Turn the ping into a colour and a label

notes: There are also avg-response (the average over a period, checking public=1 with its own SQL) and ping (through the UptimeCalculator) badges, but this flow covers the response route, which shows only the latest beat (see the notes on what could not be confirmed)
The avg-response route is a special case that does not use isMonitorPublic, so it is not expanded here

flows.title: Fetch the certificate expiry badge
flows.trigger: The live preview in the badge dialog, or a badge image pasted on an outside site, loading /api/badge/:id/cert-exp

steps.label: Live preview through the in the dialog
Copy the URL and paste it on an outside site
Look the TLS info up by monitor_id
Return whether there is a row, and its content
Pick one of three colours from the days remaining

notes: The three bands are: daysRemaining > warnDays gives upColor, > downDays gives warnColor, and anything below that gives downColor (the defaults live in badgeConstants)
With the date query it shows the expiry date (validTo) instead of the days remaining (the colour logic itself is unchanged)

flows.title: Route to the entry page
flows.trigger: Opening the SPA in a browser mounts Entry.vue, which calls /api/entry-page

steps.label: Load the domain table at startup

notes: The domain table is cached in memory as StatusPage.domainMappingList and never queried per request. It only changes when loadDomainMappingList runs again (at startup, or when a status page is saved)
A code comment in Entry.vue says the routing logic also exists on the server in production, but that was not confirmed in the files read for this map

flows.title: Prometheus collects the metrics
flows.trigger: An outside Prometheus server scrapes GET /metrics on a schedule with Basic auth

steps.label: Initialize the gauges once, at startup
Read every tag name as a label candidate
Return the metrics body in prom-client format

notes: Individual gauge values (monitor_status and the rest) are updated by the heartbeat side. For example the new Prometheus(monitor, tags).update(bean, undefined) call inside the push route (server/routers/api-router.js:132)

Where the ordinary beat loop (ping and the like) calls Prometheus.update() is not in the files read for this map (api-router.js / prometheus.js / the relevant lines of server.js / tag.js / the Vue files), so it is unconfirmed

flows.title: Create a tag
flows.trigger: Pressing "Add New Tag" on Settings > Tags, entering a name and a colour, and saving

steps.label: reset() + show() opens the dialog for a new tag
Return the tag including the generated id
Right after creating it, editTag is sent with identical content
Find the tag by id and update the name and colour
updated() refetches the list and closes the modal

notes: Even when creating a tag, an editTag with identical content is sent unconditionally right after addTag (the behaviour of TagEditDialog.vue:320-375 — redundant, but that is what the code does)
Adding or removing monitors on this screen also calls addMonitorTag / deleteMonitorTag, but that path is documented in the "Attach a tag to a monitor" flow

flows.title: Attach a tag to a monitor
flows.trigger: Choosing an existing (or new) tag in the tag UI on the monitor edit screen and saving

steps.label: Pick or type a tag and press save
emit("addTag") with the new name and colour
steps.branch: when a new tag is involved

steps.label: INSERT the new tag
steps.branch: when a new tag is involved

steps.label: Prepare the preloaded tags and the rest
Fetch the tags for the set of monitors at once
Join to get the tag names and colours

notes: Removing a tag (deleteMonitorTag) and changing its value (editMonitorTag) take the same shape of path; only the DB operation changes to DELETE or UPDATE (server/server.js:1331,1356)
Attaching only existing tags skips the addTag branch (which is for new tags) and calls addMonitorTag alone
